summary: All 28 distinct wild-type SCN genes selected in Figures 3C, S3 and S5 agree in direction with the registered scheduled-minus-unscheduled exercise coefficient. Figure 3C plots fitted fold changes for 10 genes, and the other 18 directions come from an expression heatmap or group means. Five of the 28 meet registered BH FDR < 0.05.

manualReview.summary: Wild-type SCN exercise comparison completed for 28 figure-selected genes
manualReview.note: Figure 3C labels 10 WT fold changes, Figure S3 shows the 20 top WT DE genes, and Figure S5 marks 11 WT comparisons with significant q-value brackets. These panels contain 28 distinct WT discoveries. All 28 directions agree with registered limma coefficients. Five meet registered BH FDR < 0.05. GEO identifies four mice per arm with free wheel access in the unscheduled group. The paper’s Results and S5 label the scheduled group ZT14/CT22. Its RNA-seq sample list and the GEO series design label the same mice ZT14/CT24. The publisher and PMC copies of Document S1 match byte for byte. The BioStudies file with the same name is a clinical stent supplement.
reviewFlags: The comparison covers 28 of the 795 reported WT discoveries. Only 10 have a labeled fitted-effect direction. Genome-wide overlap, exact author effects and per-gene P values and FDR remain unassessed.
The registered contrast includes differences in sampling phase and wheel schedule. The paper contains both CT22 and CT24 for the WT scheduled group. The GEO series design gives CT24.
The paper and GEO series design report GRCm38. All 14 GSM processing records report GRCm39 with GENCODE vM27. All 28 selected symbols join uniquely through deposited identifiers.
The DE table and local per-gene track each yield 81 discoveries at FDR < 0.05. The local QC summary records 1,180 for the same track.

GEO series with normalized counts and sample metadata

verificationReview.reason: Each of the 10 labeled Figure 3C fold changes and the expression directions for 18 additional figure-selected WT discoveries agrees with the sign of the registered coefficient. Five of the 28 pass registered BH FDR < 0.05. Author DESeq2 and registered limma use different models and filters. Exact author coefficients, per-gene P and adjusted P values, and the full discovery list were unavailable in the reviewed sources.
verificationReview.nextStep: For genome-wide comparison, obtain the WT SVE minus WT nSVE DESeq2 results with gene IDs, all tested and missing values, log2 fold changes, raw and adjusted P values, and the design and contrast call. Confirm the reference assembly used for alignment and resolve the CT22/CT24 sample annotation.

comparabilityReview.basis: Read the sign of labeled author log2 fold changes in Figure 3C, sample count patterns in S3, and group mean counts in S5. Compare these directions with registered limma logFC. Compare figure-defined WT discoveries with the registered BH-adjusted P values at 0.05. The GEO workbook supplies the identifiers and the counts from which the registered model was fitted.
comparabilityReview.reference: Hitrec et al., iScience 26, 106002, Figure 3C and Document S1, Figures S3 and S5. Include every labeled 3C point, every row of the S3 WT top-20 panel and every S5 gene in the WT discovery regions (c, d, e, f and i). Count each gene once across panels.

cohort.note: Four Vipr2+/+ mouse SCN RNA-seq libraries per arm. GEO, workbook columns, the registered sample sheet, model provenance and ENA agree on these eight libraries. Vipr2-null libraries are outside the registered coefficient.

contrast.note: WT scheduled wheel access minus WT unscheduled wheel access. Higher expression under scheduled exercise is positive. WT baseline tissue was collected at CT14. The scheduled group was collected at ZT14, called CT22 in the Results and S5 and CT24 in the paper’s RNA-seq sample list and GEO series design.

features.note: The figures label gene symbols. Each of the 28 has one workbook row, one versioned Ensembl ID and one registered feature for its final symbol. Fam189b maps to Entrep3 via ENSMUSG00000032657.15 and Ndufa4 to Coxfa4 via ENSMUSG00000029632.7. The WT Results text and figures spell Rgs16 alike. The paper and GEO series design specify GRCm38, while the individual GSMs specify GRCm39 and GENCODE vM27. The literal ID joins establish these selected matches.

effects.note: All 10 volcano signs, all 20 heatmap group directions and all 11 WT bar directions agree with the registered sign. The union contains 21 higher and seven lower genes. For 18 genes the figure evidence is an expression pattern or mean. The workbook check uses the same deposited measurements that feed the registered fit. Exact paired author coefficients and correlations remain unavailable.

inference.note: The paper describes DESeq2 with mean-based independent filtering, Cook’s-distance outlier handling and BH adjustment. The registered model uses limma on log2(DESeq2-normalized count + 1). Five of the 28 published WT discoveries pass registered BH FDR < 0.05 and 23 miss it. Figure S5 also places 19 named genes in regions outside the WT discovery set. All 19 fall outside the registered discovery set. Their numeric author P/FDR and filtering status remain unknown.

coverage.note: All 28 selected WT discoveries join uniquely. The paper reports 795 WT discoveries among 9,524 genes passing filtering and thresholding. The registered BH family contains 25,547 features, including 708 hidden unmapped features. The DE table and local per-gene track each contain 24,839 rows and yield 81 FDR discoveries. Five are among the 28. The other 76 have unknown author status in this comparison. The local qc_global.js summary separately lists nSig = 1,180.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use the published WT panels and fixed scheduled-minus-unscheduled direction. Compare figure-defined WT discoveries with registered BH FDR < 0.05. The 28 selected genes fall below the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30 paired genes. Genome-wide coverage and numeric author effects remain unavailable.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: The published directions agree for the selected WT genes. Five of the 28 also pass the registered FDR cutoff. This supports closure for selected results. Genome-wide effect and inference concordance remain unassessed.

The paper reports 795 WT discoveries (556 up, 239 down) and 9,524 genes passing filtering. The registered analysis tested 25,547 features after aggregation and filtering, including 24,839 published rows and 708 unmapped tested rows. The DE table and local per-gene browser bundle both yield 81 discoveries. The local QC summary reports 1,180.

openIssues: The full WT DESeq2 export and design are unavailable in the reviewed sources. Genome-wide effect magnitudes, gene-level inference and discovery overlap remain unassessed.
The same scheduled WT group at ZT14 is labeled CT22 in the Results and Figure S5 and CT24 in the RNA-seq sample list and GEO series design.
The GRCm38/GRCm39 source annotations conflict. The selected workbook-to-registry joins are exact. The alignment reference for whole-study reproduction still needs confirmation.
The local QC summary reports 1,180 significant genes. Both per-gene tables yield 81 at BH FDR < 0.05. The discrepancy is established for the local files.
